comment: Model catalogue. Every entry here is pinned: the file name, byte size and SHA-256 were read
from the mudler/parakeet-cpp-gguf file listing, where the LFS oid is the SHA-256 of the blob.
ModelInstaller checks every download against these digests and moves nothing into place that
The f16 digest was independently corroborated: a copy installed and used for three hours of
audio hashed to the same value the repository publishes.
An entry added later with "sha256": null still works, but it downloads unverified and both
the CLI and the UI say so on its face. See docs/MODELS.md before adding one.
Sizes are exact and are compared to the downloaded byte count, so a rounded value is a bug.
Weights are CC BY 4.0 (NVIDIA). Redistribution is permitted and the notice obligations are in
Licensing/Attribution.cs — they are not satisfied by attribution alone.

models.notes: The smallest step down from f16, and measured against human transcripts: 10.23% word error rate against f16's 10.21% over eleven hours of accented English earnings calls (Earnings-22 Subset 10, CUDA, 2026-08-16, docs/UNPROVEN.md) — no measurable cost on that corpus. Divergence from f16 is 0.42% of tokens over 2 h 55 m; that is which words differ, not how many are wrong. One English corpus of one genre, scored with this project's own normaliser, is the whole of the evidence: it is enough to say this entry is not the silent collapse the analogous ONNX INT8 export was, and not enough to say more. Saves about 500 MB of download and some CPU decode time.

Default choice, and the reference for accuracy: 10.21% word error rate against verbatim human transcripts of eleven hours of accented English earnings calls, 13.40% against non-verbatim ones (Earnings-22 Subset 10, CUDA, 2026-08-16, docs/UNPROVEN.md; this project's own normaliser, so not comparable to a published figure). It is the default because it was the one entry whose quality was not an open question when the choice was made; every quantisation in the catalogue has since scored within 0.08 points of it on that corpus, and whether one of them should replace it as the default is an open product decision. The cost is a 1.34 GiB download and a slower CPU decode than q8_0.

10.17% word error rate against f16's 10.21% over eleven hours of human-transcribed accented English (Earnings-22 Subset 10, CUDA, 2026-08-16, docs/UNPROVEN.md) — no measurable cost on that one corpus, which is the whole of the evidence.

10.17% word error rate against f16's 10.21% over eleven hours of human-transcribed accented English (Earnings-22 Subset 10, CUDA, 2026-08-16, docs/UNPROVEN.md) — no measurable cost on that one corpus, which is the whole of the evidence.

Smallest, and the one most likely to fail silently — which it did not: 10.15% word error rate against f16's 10.21% over eleven hours of human-transcribed accented English (Earnings-22 Subset 10, CUDA, 2026-08-16, docs/UNPROVEN.md), while differing from f16 on 2.69% of tokens over 2 h 55 m — differently right and differently wrong, not more wrong. One English corpus of one genre is the whole of the evidence.

deferredComment: Files in the same repository whose digests are recorded so a later version does not have to
re-derive them. They are NOT catalogue entries and this build cannot install or select them.
The reason they are not is licensing, not caution about quality. Every entry in "models"
carries a licence and an attribution id that resolves against Attribution.ById, because the
app shows that notice and CC BY is not satisfied by attribution alone. These two families are
not parakeet-tdt: Nemotron models commonly ship under the NVIDIA Open Model License rather
than CC BY 4.0, and realtime_eou has no stated provenance in the file listing at all. Naming
a licence for either would be inventing one, and it would put a false notice in front of a
So what is recorded is only what was read from the listing: name, exact size, SHA-256. To
promote one, establish the licence, register the attribution, and move it into "models".
